Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year did Marie Curie die?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Sodium discovered?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Ammonium chloride: Pfizer. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet E2 family based?
Embraer E-Jet E2 family: Brazil. The Embraer E-Jet E2 family is a series of four-abreast narrow-body regional jet airliners designed and produced by the Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer.
Who is credited with discovering Lynx?
Lynx (constellation): Johannes Hevelius. Lynx is a constellation named after the animal, usually observed in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Newton's law of universal gravitation?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Robert Hooke. This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.
Who is credited with discovering Pulsar?
Pulsar: Jocelyn Bell Burnell. This produces a very precise interval between pulses that ranges from milliseconds to seconds for an individual pulsar.
Who is credited with discovering Coma Berenices?
Coma Berenices: Conon of Samos. Coma Berenices is an ancient asterism in the northern sky, which has been defined as one of the 88 modern constellations.

Belonging to the birch family and numbering about 35 species, these monoecious trees and shrubs are found across the north temperate zone, with a few extending into Central America and the Andes — name this genus of tree?
Alder are trees of the genus Alnus in the birch family Betulaceae.

Usually a symptom of coronary artery disease caused by atherosclerosis narrowing the arteries, this chest pain or pressure gets its name from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest' — name this condition?
Angina is chest pain or pressure, usually caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart muscle (myocardium).

This type of blood vessel typically carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, though the vessels serving the lungs and an unborn baby's placenta carry deoxygenated blood instead — what's it called?
Artery (from Greek (artr)) is a blood vessel in humans and most other animals that takes oxygenated blood away from the heart in the systemic circulation to one or more parts of the body.
Built under license from the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, this turboprop trainer serves the US Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps and flies in Canada under the designation CT-156 Harvard — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II is a single-engined, turboprop aircraft currently built by Textron Aviation, formerly manufactured by Raytheon Aircraft Company, which sold to Textron in 2007.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
Scholars still argue whether it merely transmits meaning or also creates it, but the simplest definition of this concept is the transmission of information — what is it?
Communication is commonly defined as the transmission of information.
Named after the bladder it was first found in, which amino acid carries a thiol side chain that forms the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together?
Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HSCH2CH(NH2)COOH.
Domesticated over 14,000 years ago — before farming even began — this descendant of wolves shares a common ancestor with the modern gray wolf. What animal is it?
Dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of her country's central bank, and was ranked among Forbes' most powerful women in 2019 — who is she?
Elvira Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This term describes the practice of exposing normally covered body parts to others in public or semi-public settings, whether in person or via a nude photo shared digitally — what is it?
Exhibitionism is the practice of exposing one's intimate parts - such as the breasts, genitals, or buttocks - in a public or semi-public environment.
This American political scientist argued in a controversial 1992 book that the spread of liberal democracy and free markets might be the final form of human government — who is he?
Francis Fukuyama (born October 27, 1952) is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar.
Before he founded a piece of the U.S. aircraft industry, this pioneer set an unofficial world speed record astride a V8-powered motorcycle that stood unbroken until 1911. Who was he?
Glenn Curtiss (May 21, 1878 - July 23, 1930) was an American aviation and motorcycling pioneer, and a founder of the U.S.
Prehensile and multi-fingered, this appendage sits at the end of primates' forearms, though a few other animals like koalas and raccoons are sometimes described as having one too — which body part?
Hand is a prehensile, multi-fingered appendage located at the end of the forearm or forelimb of primates such as humans, chimpanzees, monkeys, and lemurs.
Originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East, this unit of time is now fixed at exactly 3,600 seconds — name this unit?
Hour (symbol: h; also abbreviated hr) is a unit of time historically reckoned as 124 of a day and defined contemporarily as exactly 3,600 seconds.
Once extracted from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this insoluble blue colorant is famous for dyeing denim and enabling tricks like stone washing. What is it?
Indigo dye is an organic compound with a distinctive blue color.
Born in Albuquerque and a Princeton engineering graduate, this businessman founded and once ran Amazon, the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant — who is he?

Jeff Bezos (n Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This Soviet theoretical physicist laid the foundations of twentieth-century condensed matter physics and explained the theory behind superfluid helium — who is he?
Lev Landau (22 January 1908 - 1 April 1968) was a Soviet physicist who made fundamental contributions to many areas of theoretical physics.
Its name is Latin for 'wolf,' and this autoimmune disease cycles between flares and remission, often announcing itself with a red rash across the face — what is it?
Lupus (SLE), is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in many parts of the body.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
This Soviet tandem-seat helicopter was built purely for anti-armor attack missions, carrying no secondary transport capacity unlike the gunship it succeeded — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.

Jointly operated by the U.S. Air Force and NASA in the 1960s, this rocket-powered experimental aircraft set speed and altitude records, once reaching Mach 6.7 and crossing into the edge of outer space — name this aircraft?

North American X-15 is a hypersonic rocket-powered aircraft formerly operated by the United States Air Force and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) as part of the X-plane series of experimental aircraft.
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compounds pairs oxygen with at least one other element — even the thin protective skin on aluminum foil counts as one — what's the class?
Oxide is a chemical compound containing at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.
Named from Greek words for 'odd' and 'toe,' this mammalian order groups horses, rhinoceroses, and tapirs together based on their toe count. Which order?
Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek, perisss 'odd' and, dktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.

Caused by a mutation in a single gene that holds the cell nucleus together, this rare disorder makes children age much faster than normal, with most patients living only into their teens or twenties — what's the condition?
Progeria (also Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome or Hutchinson-Gilford progeroid syndrome; HGPS) is a type of progeroid syndrome.

Cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seeds, this yellow-flowered Brassica crop is the source of a low-toxicity oil marketed under a Canadian-coined name, and ranks as the world's third-largest vegetable oil source — what is it?
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
First described in 1779, which large African raptor stands over four feet tall on stilt-like legs and is grouped in its own family, Sagittariidae?
Secretarybird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
This discipline scientifically examines human society, scaling from micro-level individual interactions up to macro-level social systems — what is it?

Sociology is the scientific study of human society that focuses on society, human social behavior, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and aspects of culture associated with everyday life.
Lacking the powder down that herons and ibises use to clean off fish slime, these bill-clattering wading birds come in 20 living species across six genera — which birds?
Stork are large, long-legged, long-necked wading birds with long, stout bills.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Divided into the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, this core section of the body is where the head, neck, and all four limbs attach — which body part?
Torso is the central part, or the core, of the body of many animals (including human beings), from which the head, neck, limbs, tail and other appendages extend.
Measuring under five feet long, this critically endangered porpoise is endemic to a small corner of Mexico's Baja California coast — which species?
Vaquita (v-; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.

Multicellular eukaryotes that breathe oxygen and grow from a hollow ball of cells called a blastula, over 1.5 million species in this kingdom have been described by scientists. What are they collectively called?
Animal: Biological kingdom. Over 1.5 million living animal species have been described, of which around 1.05 million are insects, over 85,000 are molluscs, and around 65,000 are vertebrates.
Native to the northern tundra, this small mammal grows thick white fur for winter camouflage and forms monogamous breeding pairs while preying on lemmings and seabirds — what animal is it?
Arctic fox: Species of fox. It is well adapted to living in cold environments, and is known for its thick, warm fur that can be used as camouflage against snow in the winter.
This independent examination of financial records culminates in a report expressing an opinion on whether the books are free of material misstatement — what is it called?
Audit: Independent examination of an organization. The term is most frequently applied to audits of the financial information relating to a legal person.
In continuous production since 1974 — the longest run of any civilian turboprop plane in its class — this twin-engine model also serves in medevac and flight-inspection roles — what is it?
Beechcraft Super King Air: Light twin-turboprop transport aircraft family.
Not a species of its own, it's really a melanistic leopard or jaguar whose rosettes are still hidden under the dark coat — what do we call this big-cat colour variant?
Black panther: Variant of leopard and jaguar. Black panthers of both species have excess black pigments, but their typical rosettes are also present.
This subfamily of horned, cloven-hooved ungulates includes cattle, bison, and both African and water buffalo, with the gaur as its largest living member — which group?
Jointly developed by Pakistan and China as a lightweight fourth-generation fighter meant to eventually succeed the F-16 in Pakistan's air force, this jet's Chinese designation is FC-1 — what is it?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Sino-Pakistani multirole fighter aircraft.
This medical emergency occurs when the heart suddenly stops beating effectively, cutting off blood flow to the brain and other organs within minutes — what is it called?
Cardiac arrest: Sudden or unexpected loss of heartbeat.
Latin for 'little brain,' this hindbrain structure fine-tunes motor coordination and timing without actually initiating movement — what is it?
Cerebellum: Structure at the rear of the vertebrate brain, beneath the cerebrum.
Every animal cell makes this waxy sterol — the liver most of all — and it doubles as the raw material for steroid hormones, bile acids, and vitamin D. What is it?
Cholesterol: Sterol biosynthesized by all animal cells.
Also nicknamed the 'Maybug' or 'doodlebug,' this European scarab beetle's males swarm during mating season while females stay put munching leaves that release telltale scent chemicals — which beetle?
Cockchafer: Species of scarab beetle. The cockchafer develops via metamorphosis, in which the beetle undergoes stages of eggs, larvae, pupae and adults.

Used in Chinese medicine for over 1,500 years, this genus of parasitic fungi infects insects and other arthropods, taking its name from Greek and Latin words meaning 'club' and 'head' — which genus is it?
Cordyceps: Genus of fungi. Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Developed as a 14-bed sleeper upgrade of an earlier airliner, which low-wing propeller monoplane cruised at 207 mph and reshaped air travel from the 1930s through World War II?
Douglas DC-3: Airliner and military transport aircraft family.
Capable of delivering shocks up to 860 volts, this South American knifefish helped inspire the invention of the battery in 1800 — what is it?
Electric eel: Genus of fishes in South America.
Also called rocket or arugula, this sharp-flavored leaf vegetable native to the Mediterranean and Asia is a popular salad green in the cabbage family — which plant?
This burrowing mammal builds ever-expanding tunnel systems, and its saliva contains toxins that paralyze its favorite prey, earthworms — what animal is it?
European mole: Species of mammal. The European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.
This antiandrogen medication lowers DHT production by about 70 percent and is used to treat pattern hair loss and an enlarged prostate — which drug?

Finasteride: Antiandrogen medication. Finasteride, sold under the brand names Proscar and Propecia among others, is a medication used to treat pattern hair loss and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
This Austrian economist shared the 1974 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Gunnar Myrdal for his work on how prices communicate information — who is he?
Friedrich Hayek: Austrian economist and philosopher (1899–1992)

A Belgian Catholic priest and physicist, he was first to argue that the recession of galaxies proves an expanding universe, and proposed a 'primeval atom' — the first version of the Big Bang theory. Who was he?
Georges Lemaître: Belgian scientist and Catholic priest (1894–1966)
A U.S. Navy rear admiral who helped develop COBOL, this computer science pioneer wrote what's considered the first computer manual and worked on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper: U.S. naval officer and computer scientist (1906–1992)

Coined by psychologist Edward Thorndike, this cognitive bias describes how a positive impression in one area, like someone's looks, skews our judgment of them in unrelated areas — what is this bias called?
Halo effect: Tendency for positive impressions to contaminate other evaluations.

Synthesized from the dried latex of the opium poppy, this opioid is used medically in some countries to relieve pain during childbirth or a heart attack — and its 'black tar' form is a crude, variable mix of morphine derivatives — what is it?
Heroin: Opioid analgesic and recreational drug.
The flowers of this shrub genus act as natural pH indicators, turning blue in acidic soil and pink in alkaline soil?
The world's largest jet airliner when it first flew in 1963, this Soviet quad-engine jetliner entered Aeroflot service with a Moscow-to-Montreal flight in 1967. What aircraft?
Ilyushin Il-62: Soviet long-range narrow-body four-engined jet airliner.
An Indian polymath and pioneer of radio microwave optics, he's also considered the father of Bengali science fiction — and even has a crater on the Moon named for him. Who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose: Physicist, biologist and botanist (1857–1937)
On January 26, 1926, this Scottish inventor gave the world's first demonstration of a working mechanical television system — who is he?
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Defined as exactly one cubic decimetre and rooted in an old French unit called the litron, what metric measure of volume is this?
Litre: Unit of volume. The litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used: ℓ) is a metric unit of volume.
A Russian linguist by training, this woman served two separate terms as first lady of Russia, from 2000 to 2008 and again from 2012 to 2014 — who is she?
Lyudmila Putina: Ex-wife of Vladimir Putin (born 1958)
Prized for its sweet, pine-and-citrus flavor, this perennial herb is often considered synonymous with oregano in parts of the Middle East — what is it?
Marjoram: Perennial herb. It is also called pot marjoram, although this name is also used for other cultivated species of Origanum.
Also nicknamed 'Cornish salmon,' this predatory fish is often netted alongside the Atlantic herring it preys on, and is heavily overfished across European waters — which fish?
Merluccius merluccius: Species of fish. Merluccius merluccius or the European hake is a merluccid hake of the genus Merluccius.
With over 17,000 built and flown by more than 50 countries, this Soviet-designed twin-turbine machine is the most-produced helicopter in the world — what is it?
Mil Mi-8: Family of transport helicopters.
With a pointed snout, round ears, and a scaly tail as long as its body, this small rodent species is usually distinguished from its larger cousin the rat mainly by size — which animal?
Mouse: Small long-tailed rodent. A mouse (pl. mice) is a small rodent, characteristically known to have a pointed snout, small rounded ears, a body-length scaly tail, and a high breeding rate.
Divided anatomically into vertebral, visceral, and two vascular compartments, which flexible body part connects the head to the torso and is also called the cervix or collum?
Neck: Body part that connects the head and torso. It supports the weight of the head and protects the nerves that transmit sensory and motor information between the brain and the rest of the body.
Introduced to Hawaii in 1929, this crested songbird serves as the state bird of seven US states including Ohio and Virginia — which bird?
Northern cardinal: Species of North American bird.
Found on every continent but Antarctica, these flowers can lure pollinators by mimicking female insects, and their tiny seeds depend on fungal partners just to sprout. What plant family is this?
Orchid: Family of flowering plants in the order Asparagales.
Secreted by small neck glands when blood calcium runs low, this peptide messenger raises calcium levels and boosts active vitamin D production — which one?
Parathyroid hormone: Mammalian protein found in humans.
Discovered in 1972 and used to treat scabies and lice, this pyrethroid insecticide is safe for most mammals but especially dangerous to cats, who metabolize it slowly — what is it?
Permethrin: Medication and insecticide. It is applied to the skin as a cream or lotion.
Resembling a round, tailless rabbit with short ears, this small mountain-dwelling mammal's Himalayan relative lives at elevations above 6,000 meters — what animal is it?
Pika: Genus of mountain-dwelling mammal. A pika ( PY-kə, PEE-kə) is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
This succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae has every part edible, whether raw or cooked, and is also known by folk names like little hogweed — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Portulaca oleracea: Species of plant in the purslane family.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Also called false saffron, this thistle-like annual is one of the world's oldest crops, prized today for the vegetable oil pressed from its seeds — what plant is it?
Safflower: Species of plant. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.
With over 60 types found throughout the human body, this ring-shaped muscle keeps a bodily passage closed until it relaxes to let something through — what is it called?
Sphincter: Circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid made from benzene is the precursor to polystyrene, with global production reaching some 35 million tonnes by 2018 — what compound is it?
Styrene: Chemical compound. Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.
One of the largest parasitoid wasps, this creature paralyzes its eight-legged prey with a sting, drags it into a nest, and lays a single egg so the larva can devour the still-living host. What is it?
Tarantula hawk: Common name for two genera of wasps.
Working in his famous "Fly Room" with fruit flies, this American won a Nobel for showing that genes ride on chromosomes — who was he?
Only about 76 to 90 nucleotides long, this adaptor molecule reads each three-letter mRNA codon with a matching anticodon and ferries the right amino acid to the ribosome — what is it?
Transfer RNA: RNA that facilitates the addition of amino acids to a new protein.
Element 121, this not-yet-synthesized superactinide is expected to open a brand-new g-block of the periodic table and may sit on the 'island of stability' — what's its placeholder name?
Unbiunium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 121 (Ubu)

Despite having no formal medical education, this laboratory supervisor helped develop a life-saving shunt for blue baby syndrome alongside a surgeon and a cardiologist, later earning an honorary doctorate from Johns Hopkins — who was he?
Famed for ferocity wildly out of proportion to its size, this muscular carnivore (Gulo gulo) is the largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family — what is it?
Wolverine: Species of the family Mustelidae.

Samarium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for samarium is Sm. Samarium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sm and atomic number 62.

Alan Rickman: Alan Sidney Patrick Rickman (21 February 1946 – 14 January 2016) was an English actor.
In what year was Michelle Williams born?
Michelle Williams (actress): Michelle Ingrid Williams (born September 9, 1980) is an American actress.
In what year was Christopher Reeve born?
Christopher Reeve: Christopher D'Olier Reeve (September 25, 1952 – October 10, 2004) was an American actor, activist, director, and author.

In what year was Zoë Kravitz born?
Zoë Kravitz: Zoë Isabella Kravitz (born December 1, 1988) is an American actress, singer, and filmmaker.
